findings.portabilityNote: Apptegy/Thrillshare districts serve their page content as an escaped JSON payload inside the served HTML. Any roster verifier that compares stored names against RENDERED PROSE will report a false ABSENT for every Apptegy tenant. The fix is to search the served bytes (including <script>) before asserting absence.

findings.headline: The Pima County Board of Supervisors DOES publish minutes, and the route that enumerates them is a host this repo already uses. 403 sittings 2013-04-16 to 2026-08-25; 361 of them carry a published minutes file.
findings.publisher: Granicus Legistar Web API, on behalf of the Pima County Clerk of the Board
findings.custodian: Pima County Clerk of the Board
findings.route: rung 3 — documented vendor JSON API, plain node fetch, no key

robots.verdict: NO_ROBOTS — the host publishes no restriction. Matches the standing docs/sources.md row.

measurement.pagingMethod: $top=200 with $skip=0,200,400,600 — the API caps a page at 200 and $top=2000 is HTTP 400, so the total is only knowable by paging
measurement.page600: 0 rows — the enumeration is EXHAUSTED, not truncated

artifactFields: EventMinutesFile — the URL of the published Meeting Summary PDF
EventMinutesStatusName — Draft or Final, so a reader can be told the record is not yet adopted
EventMinutesLastPublishedUTC — when the custodian last published it
walls: The EventMinutesFile VALUES point at legistar.granicus.com, which disallows everything (see D6). The METADATA is on a permitted host; the PDF BODY is not. This is a record we can name, date, status and link but must not fetch.
findings.extractionStatus: NOT_LINKED — data/meetings-snapshot.json carries agendaUrl and agendaDocuments only. No minutes field exists in the snapshot and lib/sources/legistar/types.ts declares EventMinutesFile and EventMinutesStatusName but nothing consumes them.
findings.readerQuestion: Did the Board actually meet on that date, and is there an official record of what happened?
findings.portabilityNote: Every Legistar tenant exposes the same three minutes fields. Mesa is already a second tenant in this repo and can be measured the same way.

findings.headline: WALL, AND A LIVE COMPLIANCE DEFECT: legistar.granicus.com serves 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /'. The host appears NOWHERE in docs/sources.md, and data/meetings-snapshot.json holds 16 agenda documents from it with 216,972 characters of extracted PDF text.
findings.verdict: PERMISSION, not transport. Three clients, one answer, HTTP 200 with an explicit Disallow. RULING 182 orthogonality is satisfied: this is a rule, not a fetch failure.
findings.relatedStandingRecord: docs/sources.md already records pima.granicus.com as DISALLOWED - NOT WALKED and honours it. legistar.granicus.com is a SIBLING host on the same vendor domain that was never checked, and it is the host every Pima and Mesa agenda PDF URL in the snapshot actually points at.

secondExposure.note: docs/sources.md line 632 records this host as DISALLOWED - NOT WALKED, read 2026-08-27. The 9 documents predate that read, so the discovery came AFTER the fetches. The stored text is still there.

findings.actionThisSessionTook: NOTHING was fetched from legistar.granicus.com by this session. The minutes work in D4 and D5 was done entirely against webapi.legistar.com, which is NO_ROBOTS.
findings.disposition: WALL_NAMED — reported to the integration owner as a compliance defect. This session owns no file that can remediate it.
findings.readerQuestion: n/a — this is a governance finding, not a reader fact.
findings.portabilityNote: The lesson is a rule: the host in a document URL is frequently NOT the host of the portal that listed it. Permission must be checked against the host actually fetched, per document, not per portal.

findings.headline: CODE DEFECT (reported, not fixed): lib/sources/legistar/ already calls the eventitems route that carries the outcome fields, and throws every one of them away.

evidence.lib/sources/legistar/client.ts:240-246: fetchEventItems() requests `${slug}/events/${eventId}/eventitems` — the exact route whose response carries EventItemActionName, EventItemPassedFlagName, EventItemMover, EventItemSeconder, EventItemTally, EventItemRollCallFlag and EventItemMatterStatus.
evidence.lib/sources/legistar/index.ts:371-377: toAgendaItems() maps each item down to { id, sequence, title, matterFile } only. Every outcome field is dropped at this line.
evidence.lib/sources/legistar/types.ts:41-44: LegistarEvent already DECLARES EventMinutesStatusName and EventMinutesFile. Nothing reads them.
evidence.votesRoute: No reference to a votes endpoint exists anywhere under lib/sources/legistar/.

The repo currently keeps the titles and discards the decisions.
